name: Lopinavir

fields.mechanism_of_action: Lopinavir is an inhibitor of HIV-1 protease. It prevents cleavage of viral Gag-Pol polyprotein precursors into functional proteins, resulting in the production of immature, non-infectious virus particles. Lopinavir is metabolized primarily by CYP3A; when used clinically it is co-administered with ritonavir, which inhibits CYP3A and thereby increases lopinavir plasma concentrations (FDA Kaletra label, sections 1, 11 and 12.1).
indications: HIV-1 infection, in combination with other antiretroviral agents, when administered as lopinavir/ritonavir (Kaletra) (FDA Kaletra label, section 1)
contraindications: Hypersensitivity (e.g., toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, erythema multiforme) to lopinavir/ritonavir or any ingredient, including ritonavir (FDA Kaletra label, section 4)

Co-administration with drugs highly dependent on CYP3A for clearance for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious and/or life-threatening reactions (FDA Kaletra label, section 4 and Table 3)

Co-administration with potent CYP3A inducers where significantly reduced lopinavir plasma concentrations may be associated with loss of virologic response and possible resistance/cross-resistance (FDA Kaletra label, section 4 and Table 3)
side_effects: Gastrointestinal: diarrhea (most common), nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, flatulence (FDA Kaletra label, sections 6.1 and 6.2)
General: asthenia, headache, insomnia (FDA Kaletra label, sections 6.1 and 6.2)
Metabolic: elevations in total cholesterol and triglycerides; new onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus/hyperglycemia; fat redistribution (FDA Kaletra label, sections 5.5, 5.9 and 5.10)
Hepatobiliary: hepatotoxicity, including fatalities, especially with underlying hepatitis B/C (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.4)
Pancreatitis, including fatalities (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.3)
Cardiac: PR interval prolongation; second/third-degree AV block; QT prolongation and torsade de pointes (FDA Kaletra label, sections 5.6 and 5.7)
Immune reconstitution syndrome (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.8)
Increased bleeding in patients with hemophilia (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.11)

dosage.adult: Lopinavir is not administered alone; dosing applies to the lopinavir/ritonavir co-formulation (Kaletra). Therapy-naive adults: 400/100 mg (two 200/50 mg tablets or 5 mL oral solution) twice daily, or 800/200 mg (four 200/50 mg tablets or 10 mL oral solution) once daily in patients with fewer than three lopinavir resistance-associated substitutions. Therapy-experienced adults: 400/100 mg twice daily. Tablets may be taken with or without food (swallowed whole); oral solution must be taken with food (FDA Kaletra label, sections 2.1).
dosage.geriatric: Clinical studies did not include sufficient numbers of patients aged 65 years and older to determine whether they respond differently; no specific dose adjustment is stated (FDA Kaletra label, section 8.5).
dosage.paediatric: As lopinavir/ritonavir (Kaletra) in pediatric patients 14 days and older, dosed twice daily based on body weight or body surface area; oral solution for children unable to swallow tablets. See the Lopinavir/Ritonavir monograph for full pediatric tables (FDA Kaletra label, section 2.2).

interactions: As lopinavir/ritonavir: CYP3A inhibitor and substrate; review all concomitant medications (FDA Kaletra label, sections 4, 5.1 and 7)

Contraindicated with alfuzosin, rifampin, ergot derivatives, cisapride, St. John's wort, lovastatin, simvastatin, sildenafil (Revatio) for PAH, pimozide, triazolam and oral midazolam (FDA Kaletra label, Table 3)
Dose adjustment required with efavirenz, nevirapine, amprenavir, or nelfinavir (FDA Kaletra label, sections 2.1 and 7.3)
Caution with QT-prolonging drugs and drugs metabolized by CYP3A (FDA Kaletra label, sections 5.6, 5.7 and 7)
fields.monitoring: Monitor liver function, lipids, blood glucose, and for pancreatitis and immune reconstitution (FDA Kaletra label, sections 5.3, 5.4, 5.5 and 5.10).
fields.patient_counselling: Advise that lopinavir is used only as lopinavir/ritonavir (Kaletra) and does not cure HIV. See the Lopinavir/Ritonavir monograph for full counselling (FDA Kaletra label, section 17).
warnings: Drug interactions via CYP3A inhibition (FDA Kaletra label, sections 4, 5.1 and 7)
Pancreatitis, including fatalities (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.3)
Hepatotoxicity, including fatalities (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.4)
PR/QT prolongation (FDA Kaletra label, sections 5.6 and 5.7)
Preterm neonatal toxicity from alcohol/propylene glycol in oral solution (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.2)
precautions: Once-daily administration not recommended in pediatric patients or with >=3 lopinavir resistance-associated substitutions (FDA Kaletra label, sections 2.1 and 2.2)
Oral solution must be taken with food (FDA Kaletra label, section 2.1)
serious_adverse_reactions: Pancreatitis, including fatalities (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.3)
Hepatotoxicity, including fatalities (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.4)
Life-threatening cardiac toxicity in preterm neonates receiving oral solution (FDA Kaletra label, section 5.2)
food_interactions: As lopinavir/ritonavir: tablets may be taken with or without food; oral solution must be taken with food (FDA Kaletra label, section 2.1)
fields.pregnancy_guidance: No adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry monitors outcomes (FDA Kaletra label, section 8.1).
fields.lactation_guidance: It is not known whether lopinavir or ritonavir are excreted in human milk; HIV-infected mothers should not breastfeed (FDA Kaletra label, section 8.3).
fields.overdose: No known specific antidote; supportive treatment (FDA Kaletra label, section 10).
fields.pharmacokinetics: Lopinavir is metabolized primarily by CYP3A and is 98-99% plasma protein bound; ritonavir inhibits CYP3A, increasing lopinavir exposure; half-life about 5-6 hours with ritonavir (FDA Kaletra label, section 12.3).
clinical_pearls: Ritonavir is a pharmacokinetic booster (CYP3A inhibitor) and lopinavir is always given with ritonavir (FDA Kaletra label, section 11)
Lopinavir has no standalone brand; the marketed product is Kaletra (lopinavir/ritonavir)
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: No dose adjustment required in renal impairment (FDA Kaletra label, section 8.6).
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: Not studied in severe hepatic impairment; use with caution (FDA Kaletra label, section 8.6).
fields.administration_instructions: Administered only as lopinavir/ritonavir (Kaletra): tablets swallowed whole with or without food; oral solution with food (FDA Kaletra label, section 2.1).

notes: Lopinavir is not used as a single agent; it is co-formulated with ritonavir (Kaletra), where ritonavir acts as a pharmacokinetic booster via CYP3A inhibition. Content is consistent with the Lopinavir/Ritonavir monograph; dosing details are provided in that entry.
